title: D4 BP-MWPM lower-side threshold refinement
question: Does the D4-native BP-MWPM flux curve remain decreasing with size at p_X=0.26, 0.28, and 0.30, thereby locating the crossing relative to the R6X 0.32--0.36 upper-side data?
scope: X-only D4 channel, p_Z=0, first-stage flux Boolean-union loss conditional on nonterminal histories; no charge-recovery or full two-stage threshold claim.
predecessor: R6X completes the 1000-shot upper-side refinement at p_X=0.32,0.34,0.36. R6Y supplies the missing lower-side 1000-shot anchors; combined analysis uses the same physical channel, score, dense BP recurrence, and odd sizes.
implementation: cached dense-Numba realization of the validated public-record BP recurrence, followed by the same MWPM scorer; no generic-Python BP records are mixed into this allocation.

scan_design.stage_2_selection_rule: Combine R6Y with R6X and allocate matched increments only at p_X values whose adjacent-size BP 90% risk-difference interval contains zero, and their immediate p_X neighbors, until signs resolve or the cap is reached.
inference_accounting: matched 40-vs-160 iteration sensitivity at the selected crossing neighborhood

claim_boundary: R6Y plus R6X can support a finite-size flux-crossing estimate only after their combined multi-size curve and 40-vs-160 matched stability test are analyzed. It is not the paper's full two-stage D4 threshold.
